summary: A target-level continuation of T.1: import the existing graded-map and degree-three nodes, specify their full generator, grading, naturality and uniqueness interfaces, and promote the degree-two comparison to its own target. The product of two unit classes is planned here as its own theorem (Loday, Proposition 2.2.3, with Lemma 2.2.1 and the Hopf description of K_2): it is the classical Steinberg symbol up to one sign that is fixed once on the torus, so the degree-two map is the Matsumoto equivalence followed by the normalized classical-to-Quillen comparison. Only the comparison of K.7's biexact product with Loday's plus-construction product in degree (1,1) is requested from K.7. The homogeneous Milnor quotient is supplied by the accepted T.2:symbols plan, and the classical-to-Quillen comparison in its Hurewicz normalization by the T.1 follow-up T.1/chosen-k2-comparisons, which rests on the accepted StableHomotopyKTheory H.3 plan and Tau Ceti's AlgebraicTopology roadmap. V.2 consumes the degree-three component and owns image, cokernel, exactness and injectivity. All targets are planned; the K.7 model comparison and the residual Matsumoto gaps of T.2:symbols prevent closure. Nothing is formalised.

nodes.title: Degree-two identification with the classical Matsumoto map
nodes.statement: Let F be a field. Write m_F : K₂^M(F) ≃ K₂^cl(F) for the symbol-preserving Matsumoto equivalence, {a,b} ↦ {a,b}, obtained from T.2/matsumoto through the degree-two presentation of the Milnor ring (T.2:symbols/field-proof/homogeneous-components); θ₂ : K₂^cl(F) ≃ K₂(F) for the natural comparison of T.1/k2-pi2 in its Hurewicz normalization β (T.1/chosen-k2-comparisons), transported to the Quillen model; and θ₂♮ = θ₂ ∘ (x ↦ x^ε) for its normalization by the torus sign ε of T.2/unit-loop-product-symbol. Then the degree-two component Φ₂ of the imported unital graded map equals θ₂♮ ∘ m_F. In particular Φ₂ is an isomorphism, natural in unital field homomorphisms. The identity uses the product-symbol theorem; it does not follow from bilinearity or from Matsumoto's theorem alone.
hypotheses: F is a commutative field; every symbol entry is a unit.
The degree-(1,1) comparison of K.7's biexact product with Loday's plus product is the open request used by T.2/unit-loop-product-symbol.

The imported Matsumoto node rests on the infinite-field proof inputs of T.2:symbols and keeps its recorded finite-field and stable-witness gaps; θ₂ is the Hurewicz normalization planned in T.1/chosen-k2-comparisons, which awaits its review.
proofSteps: By the imported symbol formula, Φ₂{a,b} = ι_F(a)·ι_F(b), where ι_F(a) = θ₁(K₁.ofUnits a).

The degree-two Milnor group is generated by two-symbols: homogeneous-components identifies it with the tensor quotient Q₂(F), which pure tensors generate. Two homomorphisms agreeing on symbols are equal.
m_F and θ₂♮ are equivalences, so Φ₂ is one. Naturality is transported from the graded map and the two natural equivalences; θ₂♮ is natural because ε is a constant sign.
This identifies the map already constructed and is not an input of its construction, so the descent argument is not circular.
acceptance: The equality is on the actual degree-two homomorphism, not merely an abstract isomorphism of its source and target.
At ℚ(t), the tame residue at t = 0 of (θ₂♮)⁻¹Φ₂{2,t} is 2 in T.3's convention; the reversed product or the opposite normalization gives 1/2.
Only the Matsumoto presentation, θ₂ and the product-symbol theorem give invertibility; checking relations alone does not.
For a finite field both sides vanish (Weibel III.6.1.1 and III.7.2(a)), so finite fields test nothing about the sign; the infinite fields carry the content.

nodes.title: The product of two unit classes is the Steinberg symbol
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and a, b ∈ Rˣ. The diagonal matrices D_a = diag(a, a⁻¹, 1) and D′_b = diag(b, 1, b⁻¹) are commuting elements of E₃(R), the images of h₁₂(a) and h₁₃(b), and the classical Steinberg symbol of T.2/steinberg-symbol is the commutator {a,b} = [D̃_a, D̃′_b] ∈ K₂^cl(R) of any lifts to St(R). Let θ₁ : K₁^cl(R) ≅ π₁BGL(R)⁺ be the comparison of U.6/pi1-plus-construction, θ₂ : K₂^cl(R) ≅ π₂BGL(R)⁺ the Hurewicz-route realization β_R of T.1/k2-pi2 fixed in T.1/chosen-k2-comparisons (the Hopf kernel equivalence α_R : K₂(R) ≅ H₂(E(R); ℤ), the plus-construction homology isomorphism, the inverse Hurewicz isomorphism of the simply connected cover BE(R)⁺ and the cover map), and x·y the degree-(1,1) product of Quillen K-theory of the commutative ring R (K.7's external product followed by the multiplication R ⊗ R → R). Fix the sign ε ∈ {+1, −1} by the torus convention: under the Hopf isomorphism of T.1/hopf-formula for the presentation ℤ² = ⟨s, t | sts⁻¹t⁻¹⟩, the fundamental class of Bℤ² = S¹ × S¹, oriented so that the quotient S¹ × S¹ → S¹ ∧ S¹ ≅ S² used to multiply classes of π₁ has degree one, is the class of (sts⁻¹t⁻¹)^ε. Then θ₁[a]·θ₁[b] = θ₂({a,b}^ε), naturally in R. Equivalently the normalized comparison θ₂♮ = θ₂ ∘ (x ↦ x^ε) satisfies θ₁[a]·θ₁[b] = θ₂♮({a,b}); this is the normalization under which Weibel's Example IV.1.10.1 holds literally. In particular θ₁[a]·θ₁[1−a] = 0 whenever a and 1−a are units, whatever ε is.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring (a field, for the graded map); a and b are units of R.
The product is K.7's biexact product, identified in degree (1,1) with Loday's plus-construction product by the comparison requested from GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.7.
ε depends only on the orientation of the torus, the commutator convention xyx⁻¹y⁻¹ and the Hopf isomorphism fixed in T.1; it is computed once, on ℤ², and is never chosen to force the formula.
proofSteps: Reduce to the external product. For commutative R the internal product is the external product for A = A′ = R followed by the multiplication μ : R ⊗ R → R. The comparisons θ₁ and θ₂ and the classical symbol are natural in ring maps (U.6/pi1-plus-construction, T.1/k2-pi2, T.2/steinberg-symbol), and μ sends a ⊗ 1 and 1 ⊗ b to a and b, so it suffices to compute in A ⊗ A′ with the units a ⊗ 1 and 1 ⊗ b.

Identify the product with a torus map. By the requested K.7 comparison the product of the loop classes of a and b is Loday's class [γ ∘ (a⁺ ∧ b⁺)] (Loday 2.1.10). Its composite with the quotient S¹ × S¹ → S¹ ∧ S¹ is homotopic to the unreduced γ ∘ (a⁺ × b⁺), and Loday's first display in the proof of Proposition 2.2.3 rewrites this, using that subtraction for the block-sum H-space structure is block sum with the inverse matrix, as the plus construction of Bψ for the homomorphism ψ : ℤ² → E₃(A ⊗ A′), (1,0) ↦ D_a, (0,1) ↦ D′_b. That map factors through BE⁺, the universal cover of BGL⁺ (H.3/plus-universal-cover, H.3/plus-construction-functoriality; Bℤ² is a K(ℤ²,1) by H.1/classifying-space-of-group-is-KG1).

Take Hurewicz images. BE⁺ is simply connected, so the Hurewicz map π₂ → H₂ is an isomorphism (Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology stage 8). A map S² → BE⁺ whose composite with the degree-one quotient of the torus is the torus map has Hurewicz image the image of the torus fundamental class (Loday, Lemma 2.2.1, with n = 2 and Γ = ℤ²; the fundamental class is the cross product of the circle classes, AlgebraicTopology stage 5). Through H.3/plus-integral-homology this image is ψ_*[T²] in H₂(E(A ⊗ A′); ℤ).

Pass to K₂ through Hopf's formula. T.1:classical/hopf-formula-natural, for the presentation of ℤ² and the map of free groups sending s and t to the free generators x_{D_a} and x_{D′_b} of the canonical presentation of E, sends the Hopf class of sts⁻¹t⁻¹ to the class of the free commutator [x_{D_a}, x_{D′_b}]. Under the Hopf kernel equivalence α of T.1/chosen-k2-comparisons (T.1:classical/uce-kernel-h2-natural, T.1/k2-h2-elementary) that class is the commutator of Steinberg lifts of D_a and D′_b, because in a central extension of a perfect group a commutator depends only on the images of its entries. By the definition of ε, ψ_*[T²] therefore corresponds to {a,b}^ε (Weibel III.5.10–5.10.1), and applying θ₂ gives the formula.
If a and 1−a are units then {a, 1−a} = 1 by T.2/steinberg-identity, so the product vanishes for either value of ε. This is the relation the graded map needs before it descends.
acceptance: The same ε serves every commutative ring, every pair of units and every ring map; it is determined on ℤ² alone.
Reversing the factors gives θ₁[b]·θ₁[a] = θ₂({b,a}^ε) = −θ₁[a]·θ₁[b] in additive K₂, consistent with K.7/graded-commutativity and the skew-symmetry of the classical symbol.

Loday identifies π₂BE⁺ with the Steinberg kernel through the connecting map of the extension and finds the inverse commutator (Proposition 2.2.3); his Remark on p.338 gives the Schur-multiplier route used here. T.1:plus/normalised-comparison normalizes the same inherited comparison through that connecting map (χ_A), while T.1/chosen-k2-comparisons uses Hurewicz (β_R). The two are natural equivalences with the same source and target and are compared on the torus class before either is substituted for the other; ε is defined relative to β.
For R = ℚ(t), a = 2 and b = t, (θ₂♮)⁻¹(θ₁[2]·θ₁[t]) = {2,t}, whose tame residue at t = 0 is 2 in the T.3 convention; the opposite normalization or the reversed product gives 1/2.

sources.locator: §2.1.10, printed p.335 / PDF p.28; §2.2, Lemma 2.2.1, printed p.336 / PDF p.29; Proposition 2.2.3 with its proof and the following Remark, printed pp.337–338 / PDF pp.30–31.
sources.match: The product of two degree-one classes is the plus construction of the torus map of the two commuting diagonal matrices; the lemma identifies the Hurewicz image of such a map with the image of the torus fundamental class. Under the connecting map of the Steinberg extension Loday obtains the inverse of the commutator of lifts, and his remark indicates the Schur multiplier route that this node uses to fix the sign.

api.name: milnorToQuillen
api.statement: The unique unital graded ring map Φ_F : K^M_*(F) → K_*(F) taking {u} to ι_F(u), the unit matrix class transported through the natural classical K1 comparison.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_zero
api.statement: On degree zero, n maps to n[F]. Through the canonical K0 model comparison and pinned SplitK0.finrankEquiv this is the identity of ℤ.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_one
api.statement: On degree one Φ_F equals θ1_F composed with the additive version of K1.ofUnits; composing with the field determinant equivalence gives the identity on Additive Fˣ.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_two
api.statement: The degree-two map is θ₂♮ ∘ m_F: the Matsumoto equivalence followed by T.1's comparison normalized by the torus sign of T.2/unit-loop-product-symbol. This API item is promoted to K2SymbolsBrauer:T.2/graded-map-degree-two-identification.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_symbol
api.statement: For an n-tuple of units Φ_F({u1,…,un}) is the ordered product ι_F(u1)…ι_F(un). The empty tuple maps to [F]; an identity entry gives zero.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_map
api.statement: For every unital field homomorphism f:F→E, K_*(f) composed with Φ_F equals Φ_E composed with K^M_*(f), in every degree.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_graded
api.statement: The unital algebra map preserves homogeneous degree n. Multiplication of degree p and degree q classes lands in degree p+q.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_mul
api.statement: Φ_F(xy)=Φ_F(x)Φ_F(y), with degree p+q and the canonical degree transport when x and y are homogeneous.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_unique
api.statement: Unital graded ring maps K^M_*(F)→K_*(F) agreeing on every degree-one unit symbol are equal; their degree-zero maps are fixed by unitality.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_steinberg
api.statement: If a and 1−a are nonzero, ι_F(a)ι_F(1−a) = 0. This comes from T.2/unit-loop-product-symbol and the classical Steinberg identity before the tensor map descends, and does not depend on the sign ε.

api.name: milnorToQuillen_three_symbol
api.statement: The exported degree-three component sends {a,b,c} to (ι_F(a)ι_F(b))ι_F(c). Associativity identifies the other parenthesization; no permutation is implicit.

tests.name: empty_symbol
tests.statement: Φ_F({})=[F], and its image through the pinned finite-dimensional K0 model has dimension 1. A zero map fails this test.

tests.name: unit_one
tests.statement: ι_F(1)=0 in additive K1, so every positive-degree symbol containing 1 maps to zero. The source identity is multiplicative and must not map to the graded ring unit.

tests.name: rational_unit_two
tests.statement: For F=ℚ, determinant of the classical K1 representative of Φ_1({2}) is 2. This rules out a trivial degree-one map or inversion.

tests.name: steinberg_pair
tests.statement: For a≠0,1, Φ_2({a,1-a})=0; multiplying this relation by symbols on either side still gives zero.

tests.name: oriented_rational_function
tests.statement: External sign test using the T.3 convention: at t=0 in ℚ(t), the tame residue of (θ₂♮)⁻¹Φ₂({2,t}) is 2, while reversing the product or using the opposite normalization gives 1/2. T.3 is a test consumer, not a prerequisite for constructing Φ.

tests.name: field_map_two
tests.statement: For ℚ→ℚ(t), mapping Φ_1({2}) equals Φ_1 of the mapped unit, and the same square commutes for {2,3}. The functor laws hold for identity and composite field maps.

tests.name: triple_one_and_steinberg
tests.statement: Φ_3({a,b,1})=0 and Φ_3({a,1-a,b})=0 whenever the entries exist; the ordered triple formula gives these vanishing statements without V.2.

tests.name: rational_degree_three_not_surjective
tests.statement: External computation: K3^M(ℚ)=ℤ/2 and K3(ℚ)=ℤ/48. The canonical degree-three map is injective by the theorem owned in V.2, hence not surjective. Neither computation nor injectivity is an input to constructing the map.

tests.name: rational_degree_four_not_injective
tests.statement: External computation: {−1,−1,−1,−1} is nonzero in K₄^M(ℚ), since its image in K₄^M(ℝ) is detected by the sign symbol (Weibel III.7.2(c)), but Φ₄ sends it to zero in K₄(ℚ) (Weibel Exercise IV.1.12(d), because η⁴ = 0 in the stable stems). An API that asserts injectivity of Φ in every degree fails this test; it is not an input of the construction.

proofClarifications: Send a unit u to its unit-matrix K1 class, transported by θ1. Extend the resulting integer-linear map through TensorAlgebra.lift.

Use T.2/unit-loop-product-symbol and the imported Steinberg identity to kill every degree-two generator of the two-sided Steinberg ideal. Descend through RingQuot.liftAlgHom; degree preservation uses the degree presentation of T.2:symbols/field-proof/homogeneous-components, not RingQuot alone.
The source’s universal property gives uniqueness, its degree-zero unit and symbol concatenation give multiplicativity, and naturality follows by uniqueness or generator evaluation.

The supplier chain for the actual Quillen ring is K.7/products-from-biexact-functors and its S-grid, stabilization and coherence nodes; its comparison with Loday's plus product in degree (1,1) is the K.7 request. No products are constructed here.

requests.need: Compare K.7's product with Loday's plus-construction product in degree (1,1). For rings A and A′, under the identification of the base-point component of the K-theory space with BGL(−)⁺ (K.2:plus/plus-equals-Q) and of K₁ with π₁BGL⁺ (KTheoryLowDegrees U.6/pi1-plus-construction), the degree-(1,1) part K₁(A) ⊗ K₁(A′) → K₂(A ⊗ A′) of the biexact external product of K.7/products-from-biexact-functors equals Loday's product [f]∗[f′] = [γ ∘ (f ∧ f′)] (Loday §2.1.10 and Theorem 2.1.11; Weibel IV.1.10), where γ is built from tensor products of matrices and the block-sum H-space structure. State it naturally in A and A′, with the identification S¹ ∧ S¹ ≅ S² used by K.7's sign conventions made explicit; for a commutative ring the internal product is this followed by the multiplication R ⊗ R → R. The value on two unit classes and its sign relative to T.1/k2-pi2 are planned in K2SymbolsBrauer:T.2/unit-loop-product-symbol and are not requested. K.7/products-from-biexact-functors and K.7/unit-multiplication-and-K0-tensor-comparison do not state this comparison, and the locators read here state the plus product only.

The homology cross product, giving the fundamental class of the torus S¹ × S¹ as the cross product of the two circle classes, and the statement that the quotient S¹ × S¹ → S¹ ∧ S¹ ≅ S² sends it to the generator of H₂(S²; ℤ) fixed by that identification.
The absolute Hurewicz theorem in degree two for simply connected spaces, π₂(X) ≅ H₂(X; ℤ), natural in based maps, applied to X = BE(R)⁺.

They normalize the same inherited comparison by different routes, which can differ by a sign; their reviews or the assembly must state the relation of β and χ. The sign ε here is defined relative to β.

No supplier yet states the comparison of K.7's biexact product with Loday's plus product in degree (1,1); it is requested from K.7. Until it is supplied, the product-symbol theorem, the Steinberg relation used for descent and the degree-two identification rest on that request.

sourceIssues.printed: The free tensor product R^m⊗R^n and its endomorphism matrix ring are assigned rank m+n in the introductory paragraph; the proof again uses that sum for the free module.
sourceIssues.correction: Use rank mn, and identify the endomorphism ring with M_(mn)(R). The stabilized matrices are the Kronecker tensor matrices on this product-rank free module.
sourceIssues.reason: Already m=n=1 gives a rank-one tensor product, not rank two; the source’s subsequent assertion R=E in this case itself requires rank one. The product-rank basis is indexed by pairs of basis indices.
sourceIssues.known: No accessible correction established; this record is scoped to the combined author copy, with no claim about the published edition.

review.reason: Read at printed p.227 / PDF p.235 of the checksummed author copy: the introduction to Definition 5.12 identifies R^m ⊗ R^n with R^{m+n} and E with M_{m+n}(R), and the proof of Lemma 5.12.1 speaks of automorphisms of R^{m+n}. The free module R^m ⊗ R^n has rank mn; with m = n = 1 the printed rank 2 contradicts the source's own remark that E = R in that case. The intended argument is unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: Combined author draft, Theorem IV.1.10 and Example IV.1.10.1, printed p.266 / PDF p.274, with Corollary IV.1.7.1, printed p.265 / PDF p.273.
sourceIssues.printed: The theorem says that the degree-(1,1) plus-construction product coincides with the matrix symbol product of III.5.12, and the example that the product of two unit classes is the Steinberg symbol of III.5.10; the identification of K₂ with π₂BGL⁺ used for this is given only as an isomorphism through H₂(E), with no sign convention.
sourceIssues.correction: The equality holds once the identification of K₂ with π₂BGL⁺ is normalized; under Loday's identification through the connecting map of the Steinberg extension, the product of the classes of a and b is the inverse of the commutator symbol. The convention should be stated, or the sign inserted.
sourceIssues.reason: Loday's Proposition 2.2.3 (printed pp.337–338), the result cited for the theorem, proves agreement only up to sign and computes the inverse commutator under its connecting-map identification. Loday's commutator of lifts of diag(a, a⁻¹, 1) and diag(b, 1, b⁻¹) is exactly Weibel's {a,b} by III.5.10–5.10.1, since these matrices are the images of h₁₂(a) and h₁₃(b), and for central commutators the two commutator conventions agree.

review.reason: Checked at both locators and against the rendered pages 337–338 of Loday's published paper. The statement is true for a suitable normalization, so nothing built on it changes, but a formalisation must fix the sign, as T.2/unit-loop-product-symbol does.
